<thought>From the ESI‑MS spectrum the base peak at m/z 183.0451 corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 182.0378 Da. The prominent M+2 peak (~33 % of the base peak) matches the isotopic pattern of a single chlorine atom. Removing the mass of Cl (34.9689 Da) leaves ~147.069 Da to be accounted for by C, H, N, O. The formula C₆H₁₃ClNO₃ (exact monoisotopic mass 182.0584 Da) matches the observed mass within a few mDa and reproduces the isotopic distribution, making it the most plausible molecular formula.</thought>
<final_answer>C6H13ClNO3</final_answer>
